utterances.text: You mean that it was wrapped up in boxes or covered with bags, sacks?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: Well, the merchandise was in the boot. I don't know what was there or how it was packaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You didn't see it. You didn't open up the boot?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I only had my bag and another small bag.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you give us further details about the location of the house where you spent the night -- the following night, that is, from the 14th to the 15th, and the name of the person who took you in?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: The 14th, between the 14th and the 15th, I and Ivica Kupreskic and Vlatko Kupreskic were in Baska Voda, at Radislav Simovic's. His house, owned by him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: But who is Radislav Simovic? Who was that person in respect of yourself?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: Radislav Simovic at one time had, on the road from Vitez towards Zenica, a restaurant, and we would go to the restaurant frequently. We were friends. We didn't visit one another frequently. We would usually go to the restaurant, meet up there. Before the war, a long time before the war, he went to Baska Voda, built himself an enormous house where he rents out rooms to tourists now and that's what he lives from.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: At the time, he was operating this type of an establishment? That is, in 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. The house had not been completely finished. He didn't have a facade on the house. The parts around the house weren't completed, but otherwise it was more or less completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Did you meet other people at his house?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: No. There was myself, we were there, and then there was Radislav and his wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: When you arrived, did people know you were coming? Had that been planned? Had it been planned for some time?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether Ivica and Vlatko said they were coming. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Let's speak about your return home. You told us that during the evening, after you had arrived, that is, around 6.30, after your luggage had been unpacked, which I think is something that you said, various people came to see you. Unless I'm wrong, and you'll tell me if I am, you did not mention the name of Mirko Sakic.

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I did mention Mirko Sakic, but when I returned from my mother's house, that's when Mirko Sakic came. He came for a brief moment, we said hello, said a few words and then Mirko went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: As well as you can recall, and there might be difficulty being specific about it now, given all the time that's gone by, but how long do you think that Mirko Sakic stayed in your house?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I couldn't really say, because I was very excited, having come back after over a year, and I was happy to see them all. I couldn't really say how long he was there for. He didn't stay long, at any rate.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Was Vlatko Kupreskic in your house at some point during the evening?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: No. We came together with Vlatko. He was tired, of course, and that's probably why he didn't come, and his wife came with her two children and with Vlatko's mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: As regards your three children, did they stay alone in the house when your husband came to get you in Split?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: No, they were not alone. They were with my husband's aunt and Ivica's father, with their grandfather.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You said that during the evening people had spoken a great deal about the situation in Germany, how people lived there, the resources that the country might offer. It doesn't seem that the situation in Central Bosnia, specifically in the Vitez region was the subject of much conversation, according to what you said a few minutes ago. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: The situation in Vitez was not discussed. Nobody mentioned the situation in Vitez at all. We discussed the time I had over there, how the children were homesick and wanted Ivica, and we talked about what had happened there, who got married, who had died. Those were the kind of talks we had. We didn't discuss anything about the situation in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Therefore among -- in all the conversation that you had with the people you met that evening, you never got the impression that there were problems in Vitez and in the region, or that there was some type of danger that one might foresee?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: No danger, no. Nobody mentioned any danger. Nobody could even think about any kind of danger being present.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Do you remember the fact that Commander Totic, in Zenica, had been kidnapped? Did you speak about that?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: We already heard that up at Sebisic, and we asked what had happened, that the situation, the Totic situation --

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you tell us exactly when it was that you learned that Commander Totic had been kidnapped?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: Up at Sebisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: On the 15th of April, 1993, in the afternoon hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: How did you learn that?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: Well, my husband asked what had happened, why the barricades were there, and then he explained to my husband that that was, in fact, it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: As regards the roadblock, how many did you go through when you came back, after the border? After the border, between Croatia and Bosnia, how many roadblocks did you have to go through?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: Before that roadblock at Sebisic, there were several checkpoints, just traffic control. They would ask to see your driver's licence. At Sebisic, that's what we learnt, and at Opara as well. Those were mostly Muslim inhabitants there. We were stopped by a policeman there, and he asked us where we were coming from, and Ivica said that he was taking his wife home from Germany. He asked us how we did, how we managed to pass, and we said we passed without any problems. He then asked us where are we going from, how did we dare go, and Ivica said that his mother had died, and he apologised for having taken up our time there and then let us pass on through to Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: This event that you learned in the afternoon was not something -- that event wasn't spoken about in the evening; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: Well, for a very brief moment because it wasn't essential. They were more interested in knowing about my life in Germany and in knowing how I was personally, how I had spent my time and what had happened in my absence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: As Mr. Radovic said to you, Mirko Sakic testified before this Tribunal, and said first that the wives were not there, that there was -- that was without your being there, it was a men's meeting, and that in addition, it was -- what was particularly spoken about was the situation in Central Bosnia at that time, and among other things, the kidnapping of Commander Totic. How do you explain that this very different account was given by that witness, different from yours?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I said that it was discussed but for a very brief moment. Mirko was there. I don't know how long he was there for. While Mirko was there, there was also Miro Vidovic, Franjo's son; Miroslav Pudza was there; my father-in-law was there. After that, Manda and Marica Didak and their mother-in-law turned up; and Mirjan Kupreskic's mother, Luca, came. Vlatko Kupreskic's wife and mother came afterwards, after Mirko had been.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: In order to reconcile such differing testimony, could we not assume that during that meeting that the men met by themselves, in order to talk about things related to the current situation or the future situation in Ahmici, and that you did not participate in that men's meeting?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: No. No. I said that when the men came alone without their wives, it was a sort of joke, because Ivica had got married, so they had come to Ivica, sort of thing, to have some sweet meats.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You told us that on the next day you were awakened at 4.00 in the morning by your husband, who didn't give you any reasons for having done so, but asked you to get dressed, and to wake up the children and to go to a shelter. You told us that you left the house with your children at 5.00, and that you needed about an hour to get ready and to leave the house under the emergency situation, which apparently was going on at the moment. Isn't an hour somewhat long under those circumstances?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: My husband woke me up sometime after 4.00. I don't know what time it was exactly. While I woke up the three children, while they got ready, and while I packed some food and clothes, and we left a little before 5.00. I needed 15 to 10 minutes to reach the shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Might one not think, Mrs. Kupreskic, since you used about an hour to get ready and leave the house, that it's because you knew that you had a certain amount of time to make your preparations, the preparations needed to leave the house?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Everything was unknown to me. I didn't know anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Why didn't you stop at Mirko Sakic's house, who apparently also had a safe shelter and was much closer to your house than Mr. Vrebac's house?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I don't know why I went there, but I followed my husband up to Ivica Vidovic Jozo's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Was that the first time that you went to a shelter, the time that you went to Mr. Vrebac's house?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was my first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You told us that mattresses were in the basement. Does that mean that the shelter had been readied for the morning?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: No. Everything that was there in the photograph, the couch and the -- a three-seat sofa and the mattress that was there, there was just an old mattress in part of a room. It was sort of a niche, and the mattress was on the floor. It was an old mattress. It was probably one that already had been discarded, thrown out, and there was nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Excuse me. Excuse me. What I thought -- I believe is that you had spoken about plural, several mattresses that had made ready, but I want to look at the transcript. We saw that in the basement of the house there were several rooms, and you said there was no electricity.

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: There was electricity when we got there, when we arrived, but soon after that it disappeared. What the time was, I don't know, but there was electricity for just a brief period after our arrival.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you indicate specifically what room it was that you were in, since we saw several rooms in the picture? Perhaps you could look at D13/1. Mrs. Kupreskic, it seems that we can distinguish at least two different rooms, the one that we can see on photograph 5 and 7, and the one that you see on number 6 to the left. Perhaps there were several others, but in these pictures, apparently you can see there were at least two different rooms.

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I entered at this door and was in this room, number 7, room number 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: The room, when the photograph was taken, where there was a red sofa?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: Yes, but there was -- the sofas weren't in the room. There was just an old mattress on the floor at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: People who were in the shelter on that day, you mentioned many women's names, men's names, children's names. It seems that the men that you mentioned were all people who were middle-aged or a bit older; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were elderly people. Among them was Vlatko Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Therefore, one found shelter in that shelter that is there, that is the women, the older people and Vlatko Kupreskic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Vlatko Kupreskic I saw in the morning, at about 6.00, because in the basement it was dark. I saw him in the course of the day and sometime between 5.00 and 6.00 p.m. The elderly people who were able to move about would go out into the corridor and into the hall. They would sit around smoking. Whereas the people who were ill, who were sick, they would take turns on the mattress on the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I would like you to be as specific as you can in this respect. You are telling us that you saw, at 6.00 in the morning, Vlatko Kupreskic. Where was he when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: Well, Vlatko Kupreskic, in the morning, at 6.00, brought his wife, Ljubica Kupreskic, with two children and his mother, Marica, to the shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: When you saw him, where was he?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: In the shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Where in the shelter?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: In the part I was in.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: That means in the room that you have just pointed out to us, where we see the red sofa?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: But at the same time, you're telling us that when Vlatko Kupreskic and his family arrived there, it was dark, there was no longer any light.

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: At that shelter, there were two small windows. There were only wooden boards there, so that we would have a bit of air and light. We would take off these wooden boards every now and then.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Therefore, there was no electricity. There were the windows that you can see in the picture, and the windows were blocked by boards, or almost blocked by boards. That is that the windows were closed up, or partially, at least.

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: Yes. These windows, these boards, yes. But we would take off these boards so that we would get a bit of light and a bit of air.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: But at least the light in the room must have been very weak?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, it was rather weak, but, roughly, you could see.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You said that you saw Vlatko Kupreskic and his family arrive at 6.00 in the morning, and that you saw him again during the day. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Between 6.00 and the other time during the day, you did not see him?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I did the not see him. I mentioned just now that men, those who were sickly, stayed there on that mattress. They would take turns. All of those who could walk and could sit, would go out into this hallway because there were benches there, and they would sit there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you say for sure that Vlatko Kupreskic, whom you saw at 6.00 in the morning, stayed in that house and did not leave it the way the other men did who had brought in their families? That is, for example, your husband or Mirjan Kupreskic who brought their families to that house and then afterwards left.

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I am saying that in the morning I saw Vlatko Kupreskic bring his wife, Ljubica, and his two children and his mother in. I saw him in the evening between 5.00 and 6.00 p.m. I did not see him after that, but possibly he could have been in that hallway where the healthier men were, where they sat on those benches.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Terrier, excuse me --

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you will allow me to ask one final question, and I think that most of the questions I want to ask have been asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: A final question and then that will be all. As you will be too. You told us that in the afternoon your husband, Ivica, brought you some food, that Mirjan had done the same thing for his family. Where did they go to get that food?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: Ivica -- well, at my home was the aunt who was born in 1924, and this old lady had sent in this food for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam. Mr. President, I don't have any other questions. Again, maybe Mr. Radovic's questions, but I don't have any further ones. No, I have no more questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: You have finished with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I thank the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Radovic, I take it you have quite a few questions in re-examination? How many?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I do not. I do not. I do not have any additional questions, but just one more thing. I would like to tender into evidence the exhibits that I had asked to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. There is no objection, so these documents are admitted into evidence. I am also happy because Mrs. Kupreskic then can be released and go back home. Thank you, Mrs. Kupreskic, for giving evidence in court. You may now be released. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Before we adjourn, let me just tell you that we will resume on -- as you know, on the 15th of March with our next witness, Mr. Ivica Kupreskic, I imagine, and we will go on until the 25th. We will not be sitting on Friday the 26th of March. However, we will be sitting twice on Wednesday the 24th, from 9.00 to 1.00, and from 2.30 to 5.30. That means that you can go back home already on Friday. I hope this will be pleasant news to you. We will, as I say, stick to our programme except for this small change. All right. So we adjourn now until the 15th of March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
